title: I am training a LoRA for creating pixel art characters.
author: HarryHaka
selftext:
This was the first successful test in training an SDXL LoRA for creating pixel art. It was a long training process 14,000 steps, spanning two days. 

The dataset consists of 195 example images not a huge amount yet the results were quite interesting, the pixel art followed the style of the training data, though it’s not quite the final result I’m aiming for. 

The next step is to train a model for a longer duration using a larger dataset.  
  
So, what do you think?

comments.author: Ill-Ant-9489
comments.body: These look great, the style really came through. Quick thing on flexibility, did you caption the set or leave the tags empty? For a style lora the captions decide a lot, you want them describing the content (character, pose, what's in frame) and deliberately leaving the words pixel art out, so the look binds to your trigger instead of leaking into every tag. There's a free tool I made (mine) built around that dataset and caption step, https://github.com/perfectgf/lora-dataset-studio . Also 195 clean images is already plenty, a style usually lands near 50 steps an image, so 14k over two days is edging into overbake where the lora stops generalizing to new characters.

replies.author: HarryHaka
replies.body:
So man, I create the captions for each image in the dataset you know, I'm using a local AI in my computer to look each image and write a caption for him, I'm using Gemma4 for this. Regarding the train method, I'll change some settings, increase the batch size, gradient, learning rate, etc to try improve the style and I want to collect more data to train anoter styles or maybe the same style but each lora focus on mosters, warrior, civil people, etc.

Thanks for your comment, I really appreciate this, and of course I'll take a look in your project too.
